# Search baseline — tecnoriasl.com (Search Console, 2026-11-05)

**Source of every number in this file:** `docs/growth/_team/gsc-baseline.json`, generated by
`node scripts/gsc-query.mjs baseline` at `queriedAt = 2026-11-05T01:02:24.127Z`, for property
`sc-domain:tecnoriasl.com` with service account `guiatv-gsc@guia-tv-8fe3c.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
The index-status table in §7 was produced separately, the same day, with
`node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect <url>` (URL Inspection API).

Nothing in this document is estimated, projected or copied from another report. Where a cell has no
data it says **`sin datos`**. Percentages marked “derived” are arithmetic on the numbers shown in the
same table; everything else is an API field copied verbatim.

Windows (as computed by `scripts/gsc-query.mjs:103-106`: `startDate = today-(N-1)`, `endDate = today`,
with today = 2026-11-05):

| Label | Window | Dates |
|---|---|---|
| `d7` | last 7 days | 2026-10-30 → 2026-11-05 |
| `d28` | last 28 days | 2026-10-09 → 2026-11-05 |
| `d90` | last 90 days | 2026-08-08 → 2026-11-05 |
| `d480` | last 480 days | 2025-07-14 → 2026-11-05 |

The API returns web-search data only (no `searchType` is sent, so the default `web` type applies).
Discover, Google News and Image results are **not** part of these figures.

Two observations that are facts, not recommendations:

## 6. Sitemap state vs index reality

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Sitemap | `https://tecnoriasl.com/sitemap.xml` | `gsc-baseline.json → sitemaps[0].path` |
| First submission (before this milestone) | `2026-03-12T18:29:06.613Z`, `submitted: "24"`, `lastDownloaded: 2026-04-28T12:39:53.371Z` | discovery report §5.3 |
| Re-submitted 2026-11-05 | `PUT` → **HTTP 204**, then `isPending: true` | captain's run, 2026-11-05 |
| `lastSubmitted` after the PUT | `2026-11-05T01:02:18.646Z` | `sitemaps[0].lastSubmitted` |
| `lastDownloaded` | `2026-11-05T01:02:19.622Z` (~1 s after submission) | `sitemaps[0].lastDownloaded` |
| `isPending` at 01:02:24Z | `false` | `sitemaps[0].isPending` |
| Sitemap contents | `{type: "web", submitted: "32", indexed: "0"}` | `sitemaps[0].contents[0]` |
| Errors / warnings | `"0"` / `"0"` | `sitemaps[0].errors` / `.warnings` |
| Re-checked 01:12:32Z | identical to the row above | `node scripts/gsc-query.mjs sitemaps` |

The `indexed: "0"` counter is **stale legacy telemetry and contradicts the URL Inspection API** for the
same property on the same day:

| URL (from the submitted sitemap) | URL Inspection 2026-11-05 |
|---|---|
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/` | `Submitted and indexed` (PASS) |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios` | `Submitted and indexed` (PASS) |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios/desarrollo-software-medida` | `Submitted and indexed` (PASS) |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-desarrollar-software-medida` | `Submitted and indexed` (PASS) |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/contacto` | `Submitted and indexed` (PASS) |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/productos/talkaris` | `Discovered - currently not indexed` (NEUTRAL) — *earlier the same day: `URL is unknown to Google`; see §7* |

Both facts are true at the same time: the sitemap counter says `0` indexed URLs while the URL Inspection
API says five of the six inspected URLs are indexed. The counter therefore cannot be used as a coverage
metric (and it is reported by the API as legacy telemetry) — for coverage, inspect URLs and use the
`coverageState` values in §7. “Submitted” describes transport, not indexation: the sixth URL is in the
very same sitemap and has never been crawled.

## 7. Index status per URL (URL Inspection API, 2026-11-05)

Command shape: `node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect <url>`; fields copied from
`inspectionResult.indexStatusResult`. All six calls returned `HTTP 200` against
`sc-domain:tecnoriasl.com`.

| URL | `coverageState` | `verdict` | `lastCrawlTime` | Google canonical | crawled as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/` | Submitted and indexed | PASS | 2026-11-05T00:45:38Z | `https://tecnoriasl.com/` | MOBILE |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-desarrollar-software-medida` | Submitted and indexed | PASS | 2026-10-18T20:26:56Z | same URL | MOBILE |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios/desarrollo-software-medida` | Submitted and indexed | PASS | 2026-09-26T04:58:46Z | same URL | MOBILE |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/contacto` | Submitted and indexed | PASS | 2026-09-26T18:40:41Z | same URL | MOBILE |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios` | Submitted and indexed | PASS | 2026-10-25T23:21:18Z | same URL | MOBILE |
| `https://tecnoriasl.com/productos/talkaris` | **Discovered - currently not indexed** | **NEUTRAL** | `sin datos` (field absent — never crawled) | `sin datos` | `sin datos` |

For the five PASS rows: `robotsTxtState: ALLOWED`, `indexingState: INDEXING_ALLOWED`,
`pageFetchState: SUCCESSFUL`, and `userCanonical` equals `googleCanonical` in every case (no canonical
conflict). For `/productos/talkaris` the state fields came back `*_UNSPECIFIED`.

### 7.1 `/productos/talkaris` — the state changed between observations (keep both literals)

The `coverageState` field is not a permanent label for a URL that Google is still resolving. Three
observations the same day, all against `sc-domain:tecnoriasl.com`, all `HTTP 200`:

| # | Observed at (UTC) | `coverageState` | `verdict` | `lastCrawlTime` | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | during the D1 verification window, `2026-11-05 01:02–01:20Z` (exact per-call time not recorded) | `URL is unknown to Google` | `NEUTRAL` | absent | all `*_UNSPECIFIED` |
| 2 | `2026-11-05T01:24Z` (captain's re-check) | `Discovered - currently not indexed` | `NEUTRAL` | absent | not recorded |
| 3 | `2026-11-05T01:25:29Z` (this repair, re-run) | `Discovered - currently not indexed` | `NEUTRAL` | absent | `sitemap: ["https://tecnoriasl.com/sitemap.xml"]`, `referringUrls: ["https://tecnoriasl.com/"]`, `indexingState` / `pageFetchState` / `crawledAs` `*_UNSPECIFIED` |

Observation 3, verbatim from the API (`inspectionResult.indexStatusResult`):

```json
{
  "verdict": "NEUTRAL",
  "coverageState": "Discovered - currently not indexed",
  "robotsTxtState": "ROBOTS_TXT_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "indexingState": "INDEXING_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "pageFetchState": "PAGE_FETCH_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "sitemap": ["https://tecnoriasl.com/sitemap.xml"],
  "referringUrls": ["https://tecnoriasl.com/"],
  "crawledAs": "CRAWLING_USER_AGENT_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

**How to read this.** Neither literal is “wrong”: the field moved because Google was still resolving the
URL between calls. The two values describe different stages of the same non-indexed state —
`URL is unknown to Google` means Google had not registered the URL at all, while
`Discovered - currently not indexed` means Google now knows it (from the submitted sitemap and from a
link on `/`) but has not indexed it yet. The absence of `lastCrawlTime` in all three observations is
the stable fact.

**The substantive conclusion is unchanged:** `/productos/talkaris` is **not indexed and has never been
crawled**, even though it sits in the sitemap submitted on 2026-11-05 (`sitemaps[0].lastSubmitted =
2026-11-05T01:02:18.646Z`). Discovery, not ranking, is the current gap; re-inspect weekly and record the
literal each time rather than overwriting the previous one.

Note also `/` was crawled at `2026-11-05T00:45:38Z`, i.e. about 17 minutes **before** the sitemap
re-submission at `01:02:18Z` — Googlebot was already active on the site; the submission did not cause
that crawl. The blog article's last crawl (`2026-10-18T20:26:56Z`) is 18 days older than the baseline.

## 8. Domain-property side effect: legacy subdomains

`sc-domain:tecnoriasl.com` is a **domain property**, so GSC reports every subdomain. The 28-day page
table contains six rows from two legacy hosts:

| Host | Pages in the 28-day page table | Impressions | Clicks | Content |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `clientes.tecnoriasl.com` | 4 (`/`, `/es/home-espanol/`, `/unlock-lucrative-global-trade-opportunities/`, `/zh/home-中文-中国/`) | 9 | 1 | old client portal pages, including a Chinese-language home and an English trade landing page |
| `cms.tecnoriasl.com` | 2 (`/2024/01/18/top10-mangas-seinen/`, `/2024/01/27/robert-downey-jr-…/`) | 11 | 0 | an old WordPress blog (manga and celebrity posts) |

The query noise follows the same hosts: `manga seinen`, `mejor manga seinen`, `mejores mangas seinen`,
`mejores seinen`, `mejores seinen manga`, `seinen manga` (9 impressions) match
`cms.tecnoriasl.com/2024/01/18/top10-mangas-seinen/` (10 impressions at position 55.7); `ria`,
`ria cerca de mi`, `empresa ria` (4 impressions) are consistent with the `clientes.` portal titles.

Consequences that are facts: 20 of 216 impressions (9.3 %, derived) and 1 of 3 clicks are outside the
marketing site; the domain property's aggregate position (19.92) mixes these irrelevant pages in; and the
`cms.` WordPress posts still receive impressions (10 of them from one manga post at position 55.7).

## 10. What the 16-month window adds (and its limits)

`totals.d480` = 78 clicks / 34 810 impressions, avg position 51.88, CTR 0.22 % (derived).

`gsc-baseline.json → sixteenMonthQueries` is capped at `rowLimit: 100` (`scripts/gsc-query.mjs:110`), so
it is a **top-100 list, not the full query set**: those 100 rows sum to 7 892 impressions and 10 clicks —
22.7 % of the 34 810 impressions and 12.8 % of the 78 clicks (derived). The remaining ~77 % of
impressions are in queries outside the returned rows.

Top 12 of that list, as recorded:

These are dominated by `agencia …` and `desarrollo web galicia` phrasing that is **not** the current
positioning (software a medida / automatización / IA). `apps/web/src/app/site/seo-route-manifest.ts`
`LEGACY_REDIRECTS` contains 301s for `/agencia-de-funnels`, `/agencia-de-marketing-contenidos`,
`/agencia-adwords`, `/agencia-seo-local`, `/agencia-de-linkbuilding` and ~30 more, which is consistent
with these impressions coming from legacy URL history now redirected — a hypothesis, not a measured
cause (GSC's query list carries no landing-URL dimension in this baseline).

## 11. What this baseline cannot say

- **No GA4 numbers at all.** Sessions, engagement, conversions and lead counts are not in this file.
  GA4 admin/data access is blocked (Analytics Admin API disabled in project `533857766582`; no GA4
  property membership). See `docs/growth/GSC-SETUP.md` §8.
- **No conversions.** GSC does not know about form submissions; 3 clicks over 28 days is a search-click
  count, not a lead count.
- **No full query coverage.** 47 of the 216 impressions are unattributed at query level; the 480-day
  query list is capped at 100 rows.
- **No reliable page totals.** Page rows over-sum (251 vs 216) — do not aggregate them.
- **No index-coverage totals.** Only six URLs were inspected. There is no “how many pages are indexed”
  number in this baseline; the sitemap `indexed` counter is unusable.
- **No ranking history or trend.** Windows are independent snapshots; this file cannot say whether a
  position improved or declined.
- **No Discover/News/Image data.** Default web search type only.
- **No CTR benchmark.** A CTR of 0 % at position 16 is expected by construction (almost nobody clicks
  page 2); the file cannot say what CTR would be attainable at that position.
- **No revenue, no attribution, no brand-vs-non-brand traffic split beyond the classification in §3**
  (which is analyst judgement over GSC query strings, not a Google label).
- **No causal claim.** Nothing here shows *why* positions are 16–37 or why the 131-impression article
  gets no clicks (title/snippet/intent mismatch, SERP features, cannibalisation are all untested).
- **Data is still settling.** `dataState: "all"` was used, so the last 2–3 days can change; the 7-day
  window is the most volatile row in §1.

---

## 12. Prioritised next observations for GROWTH-03 (hypotheses, not findings)

Everything below is a **hypothesis derived from the numbers above**, together with the observation that
would confirm or kill it. None of it is a measured result, and none of it is a recommendation to change
code, copy or content.

| # | Hypothesis (from the numbers) | Observation that would test it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The pricing intent is already visible to Google but the result is not competitive: four phrasings of “precio / cuánto cuesta” hold **117 impressions at positions 16.4–36.8 with 0 clicks**. The page carrying them is presumably `/blog/cuanto-cuesta-desarrollar-software-medida` (131 impressions, position 22.3). | Re-inspect that URL's title, H1 and snippet against the query phrasing; then compare 28-day GSC impressions/clicks/position for the same query set before vs after any change. Until that comparison exists, this stays a hypothesis. |
| 2 | Google's chosen page for pricing demand may be the blog article rather than a commercial page: `/servicios/desarrollo-software-medida` has only **2 impressions at position 42**, while the blog article has 131 at 22.3. | Query the 28-day page×query cross-tab (not in this baseline) to see which URL actually ranks for the four pricing queries. |
| 3 | The `http://` variant (18 impressions, position 10.6) still competes with `https://` (33 impressions) inside the property despite the edge 301. | Inspect the http URL with `gsc-query inspect` and watch whether its impressions fall to 0 over 28 days. |
| 4 | Legacy subdomains distort the property-level average position: 20 impressions come from `clientes.` / `cms.` content (manga, Chinese portal, trade landing) at positions 1–59. | Decide whether to keep those hosts inside the domain property; re-measure the aggregate position after excluding them. |
| 5 | `/productos/talkaris` is not merely “not indexed” but **never crawled** even though it is in the submitted sitemap — so discovery/indexation, not ranking, is the current gap. Its `coverageState` already moved once the same day (`URL is unknown to Google` → `Discovered - currently not indexed`, §7.1), so treat the literal as a moving status, not a verdict. | Re-inspect weekly; the expected progression is `Discovered - currently not indexed` → `Submitted and indexed` (possibly via `Crawled - currently not indexed`). Record each literal with its UTC timestamp; nothing else can be inferred until it moves. |
| 6 | Desktop carries 84.7 % of impressions at position 22.3 while mobile carries 14.8 % at position 5.72 — the ranking difference is large enough that it may be a query-mix artefact rather than a device problem. | Pull the 28-day `device` × `query` cross-tab; if the same queries rank differently per device, it is a real device gap. |
| 7 | Brand demand is tiny but converting: 22 brand-shaped impressions produced 2 of the 3 clicks. Non-brand demand is 131 impressions and 0 clicks. | Track brand vs non-brand clicks monthly with the same classification (§3) to see whether non-brand clicks ever appear at these positions. |
| 8 | The 16-month tail is legacy positioning (`agencia …`, `desarrollo web galicia`) that the redirect map has retired; it inflates the 480-day totals without reflecting current pages. | Use 28/90-day windows for decisions and the 480-day window only as history; re-run `baseline` after 30 days to see how much of the legacy tail decays. |

## 13. How to reproduce this file

```powershell
$env:GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS = "$env:USERPROFILE\.guiatv\gsc-service-account.json"
# No property variable needed: gsc-query.mjs pins sc-domain:tecnoriasl.com and ignores a
# differing ambient GSC_SITE_URL with a warning (see GSC-SETUP.md §2).
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs baseline --out docs/growth/_team/gsc-baseline.json

# index status (§7), six read-only calls
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/"
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-desarrollar-software-medida"
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios/desarrollo-software-medida"
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/contacto"
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/servicios"
node scripts/gsc-query.mjs inspect "https://tecnoriasl.com/productos/talkaris"
```

If `baseline` is re-run, it overwrites the JSON in place. Keep the old file (copy it with a date suffix)
before overwriting if a report or review depends on the previous numbers.
